label: Last copy step (re-input of 2nd original token) in very short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original or delimiter steps. About 91% of activation mass falls on recall_idx == 2, the step where the model has just re-input original token 1 and outputs original token 2. Nearly all of that is in short sequences: L=3 (where this is the final step, about 71% of mass, top activations around 1.0) and L=4 (about 20% of mass, weaker). It is basically silent for L >= 5 apart from a small cluster at L=9, recall_idx 3 (t=12, about 6% of mass). Within L=3/4, whether it fires and how strongly depends on token identity: it is strong when the input (orig(1)) or first token is one of c, 0, w, u, q, b, d, o, and it stays silent for many others (e.g. r, h, p, k). I did not find a clean rule for which tokens count. The simple predicate gets 64% precision on L=3; adding L=4 raises recall but costs precision unless a token list is added. Magnitudes are tiny in absolute terms (max 0.004).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: 0, w, c, d; t=16: 0, w, q, g; t=6: 0, c, w, d) and the first original token (most: u, 0, c, q, n, w; least: s, x, i, r); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, L=4 & t=6.
